text:
alex: heads-up — after the kernel-routing change rolled yesterday we started seeing sporadic OOMs on nightly perf runs for long-chat workloads. repro attached in logs, memory ladder looks like a bunch of small allocations that never get reclaimed.

maria: can you paste the allocator knob settings from the job that hit OOM? expandable_segments / max_split_size_mb / garbage_collection_threshold?

alex: job config snippet:
```
expandable_segments: true
max_split_size_mb: 128
garbage_collection_threshold: 0.85
workspace_initial_mb: 512
```
The run is 10 concurrent sessions of 8k tokens, kv-cache heavy.

kevin: hm that garbage_collection_threshold is pretty aggressive (0.85 means GC happens late). With many small KV writes fragmentation can spike before GC kicks in. Try lowering to 0.6 or 0.5 to force earlier reclamation. Also max_split_size_mb=128 might cause lots of small slab splits.

rachel: noted. Another angle — the kernel routing change moved some attention kernels to the new fused path which increased transient peak allocations because it creates temporary buffers before reuse. If allocator can't merge reclaimed free regions quickly you see the surge.

alex: attached nvprof snapshot (short):
```
[GPU memory timeline] 0s: 1.2GB free
0.12s: allocations +3.8GB (many ~32-64KB)
0.15s: fragmentation holes but no contiguous 4GB block -> OOM
```

maria: can you run the small reproducer with `--allocator-debug=alloc-map`? need the free-list heatmap. Also try `max_split_size_mb=512` — larger split means fewer meta operations, may help for KV-heavy workload.

kevin: alternative is enabling buffer reuse for KV cache warmup path. We have a flag `--kv-reuse=true` that pins a small pool for common chunk sizes. That avoids creating tons of short-lived allocations. Worth trying before bumping split size.

alex: running two quick tests now: (A) gc=0.6 + kv-reuse=false, (B) gc=0.85 + kv-reuse=true + max_split_size_mb=128. Will paste timings.

ci-bot: deploy-canary: kernel-routing-v2 deployed to canary pool at 2026-03-18T09:22:10Z :rocket:

rachel: FYI if B passes, it only masks the failure; we should still tune GC and consider coalescing free-list merges on the allocator fast-path. There's a known 1-2ms window where adjacent free nodes aren't merged because the reclaim callback is deferred to GC.

alex: test results: A failed at ~60s (OOM). B survived the run but had 8% higher tail latency. Logs: `kv-reuse` reduced new allocations by ~72% but increased average workspace high-water mark.

maria: ok that lines up — reuse reduces churn but increases sustained footprint. For production we want predictable tail, so I'd prefer lowering GC threshold + enabling kv-reuse + slight workspace bump. Suggested config: 
```
expandable_segments: true
max_split_size_mb: 256
garbage_collection_threshold: 0.6
workspace_initial_mb: 768
kv_reuse: true
```

kevin: +1. Also add a quick guard in the kernel router to avoid switching to the new fused kernel when estimated transient alloc > X% of workspace (simple heuristic). That avoids the pathological fused path for very long sequences.

rachel: can we run a matrix overnight: {gc: [0.5,0.6,0.7]} x {max_split: [128,256,512]} x {kv_reuse: [true,false]} on the canary pool? I'll kick it off if you approve.

alex: please run it. repro script: `./scripts/repro_longchat.sh --concurrency 10 --seq-len 8192 --profile nvprof`

maria: one more note — set `ALLOC_LOG_LEVEL=debug` for the runs to capture split/merge ops. That will produce a lot of logging but the heatmap helps root cause.

kevin: small mitigation PR idea: when doing a split, prefer allocating from tail of large free blocks (best-fit-last) to reduce fragmentation of lower addresses that are needed for large contiguous allocations. I'll draft it.

alex: thanks. adding test outputs to: https://perf.internal/redwood/alloc/2151234567 (dash for internal tracking)

rachel: nice. if the matrix shows a sweet spot we should roll to canary with gradual ramp and a rollback window.

alex: will update by morning with matrix results. thanks all :thumbsup:
